r: German Lutheran of the **Danish-Halle (Tranquebar) Mission**; **first to translate the Bible into Telugu**
Learnt Telugu from 1719; begun 1727, completed about **1732**; printed at **Halle (Germany)** in **1746-47**
**First book printed in Telugu = the Bible**
Helped Schulz; ran a mission school at Visakhapatnam; wrote **Vedanta Rasayanam**
German pietist; founded the **Danish-Halle Mission, Tranquebar (1706)**; New Testament in **Tamil**
**Baptists**; worked from Danish Serampore to bypass Company bans; **first Telugu Bible printed in India (1807-10)**; **Serampore College 1818**
Earliest lasting **Protestant** mission in South India
**Educational and linguistic** (start of printed **Telugu prose**); trade impact negligible
**Tranquebar (Tharangambadi)**, near Tanjore, Tamil Nadu – first Danish settlement
**Serampore** (near Calcutta) – centre of Danish activity in Bengal
Serampore and Tranquebar **sold to the English (British)** under Governor-General **Hardinge I** – Danes left India

1.x: Order of arrival in India: **Portuguese → Dutch → English → Danes → French**; the Portuguese came first (1498) and left last (1961, Goa, Daman, Diu).
**Pulicat (1621):** the English briefly joined the **Dutch** there (Treaty of Defence, 1619) – abandoned due to Dutch hostility.
